title: App Service Overview
description: Understand App Service plans, environments, deployment methods, and supported runtime stacks.

data.text: Azure App Service is a fully managed platform for hosting web applications, REST APIs, and mobile backends. You bring your code; Azure handles the operating system, load balancing, and security patches.

An App Service plan defines the compute resources (CPU, memory, disk) for your app. Multiple apps can share the same plan, which saves money. Plans come in different tiers: Free, Shared, Basic, Standard, Premium, and Isolated.

data.title: Common Plan Tiers
items: **Free / Shared** — For testing. Limited CPU and no custom domains.
**Basic** — Production-ready, supports custom domains and SSL.
**Standard** — Adds autoscale, staging slots, and daily backups.
**Premium** — More instances, faster hardware, and private endpoints.
**Isolated** — Runs in a dedicated virtual network with maximum isolation.

data.text: App Service supports many languages out of the box. You usually do not need to install anything on the server.

rows: ASP.NET Core web APIs and MVC apps

data.text: Create an App Service Plan with Azure CLI

data.title: Azure CLI — Create an App Service Plan
data.content: Create a Standard S1 App Service Plan in East US
data.code:
# Create an App Service plan
az appservice plan create \
  --name MyAppPlan \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --location eastus \
  --sku S1 \
  --is-linux

data.title: Linux vs Windows Plans
data.text: Use --is-linux for Linux-based plans, which support .NET, Node.js, Python, Java, and PHP. Omit it for Windows-only plans.

terms.definition: A set of compute resources (VMs) that host one or more App Service apps.
A single VM instance within an App Service plan. Scaling out adds more scale units.
The programming language and version your app runs on, such as .NET 8 or Node.js 20.
A fully isolated and dedicated environment for running App Service apps at high scale.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Service is a managed platform for web apps and APIs.
An App Service plan defines the compute resources and pricing tier.
You can host multiple apps on a single plan to save costs.
App Service supports .NET, Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, and Ruby.
data.takeaway: App Service is usually the best starting point for a new web application on Azure.
